Alex: Heads up — prod (dedicated) is throwing NoClassDefFoundError: com/google/gson/Gson from our kotlin-client fat JAR after we added jackson-module-kotlin. Only in prod, can't repro locally. Anyone run into gson/jackson + shading weirdness with OkHttp?
Priya: @Alex sounds like a relocation/merge problem with shadowJar. If only one of the libs is relocated callers can still try to load the original package. Try relocating both and merge service files. Example: 
```gradle
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'redwood.shaded.com.google.gson'
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'redwood.shaded.com.fasterxml.jackson'
  mergeServiceFiles()
}
```
Mike: Also watch META-INF/services — jackson modules register via service loader. If you don't merge, the module won't be discovered at runtime and you'll get strange serializer fallbacks.
Mike: Separate but possibly related: we once had auth headers dropped on retries because RetryInterceptor replayed a streaming request and the body couldn't be rewound, so AuthInterceptor ended up not running on the replay. Reordering interceptors fixed it for us. Example ordering: 
```kotlin
client.newBuilder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())  // auth before retry
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor())
  .build()
```
Samir: Small gotcha — if kotlinx-serialization and jackson-module-kotlin are both on the classpath (kotlin multiplatform setups), reflection fallback sometimes prefers a different mapper. We made the mapper explicit: 
```kotlin
val mapper = jacksonObjectMapper().registerModule(KotlinModule())
```
Samir: We also had a workaround where we forced early classloading of shaded classes during startup to surface errors in CI instead of prod: `Class.forName("com.google.gson.Gson")` — hacky but useful for debugging.
Alex: I'll try relocating both packages + mergeServiceFiles and register the KotlinModule explicitly, + reorder interceptors. Will report back with a minimal repro if it persists. :thumbsup:
